\label{ch:and_or}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=white, colframe=secondaryblue, boxrule=1pt, arc=2mm]
\textbf{\large\textcolor{primaryblue}{AND only loses bits and OR only gains them: monotone chains, the submask order, and the few distinct values they reach.}}

\begin{plannedbox}[Planned Contents --- this chapter is not written yet]
\textbf{Part A --- Lessons}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{A\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item Monotonicity: $a \,\&\, b \le \min(a, b)$, $a \mid b \ge \max(a, b)$, and at most $\log V$ changes along a chain
    \item The submask partial order: $a \subseteq b \iff a \,\&\, b = a \iff a \mid b = b$
    \item AND and OR of a range of integers $[l, r]$: the common prefix
    \item Raising AND with a budget of increments; making OR reach a target
    \item Closure under OR: the set of values reachable by OR-ing elements
\end{enumerate}
